chapter: Arranging, Fletcher Henderson and Lucky Millinder
title: Writing in Buffalo and Count Basie's offer to be his arranger
summary: He recalls his exciting writing period in Buffalo and that Count Basie, who knew him from Colorado Springs, offered him a place as regular arranger.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: In fact we scuffled through that, that's one of the things that didn't come off too good. We did that for another album, another recording company in New York before we went on tour. But what I'm saying, it was during this period I had all this experience with Coleman Hawkins and I was learning. And of course I forgot to tell you about the period in Buffalo before I came to New York, which was my most exciting period in writing music, you know. We talked about everything but that.

And before I came to join Lester Young in New York I had written for a number of bands, you know, from time to time, and I had written some things for Count Basie that he liked very much. Because at that time Count Basie was looking for all kinds of music to be played, because, you know, Basie had a lot of ideas but he didn't have time to write them and he always got other people to write them. And because of this warm relationship I had with Count Basie, who I told you knew me when I was a kid, in Colorado Springs, when he was with Bus Moten, because of that relationship and the connection I had with Joe Jones and Lester Young playing with them, the other guys who heard about me writing arrangements with Nat Towles Fells and these other people, Count Basie made me an offer to join his band as an arranger, a regular arranger.
